ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A flow cytometer can separately count cells according to differences in the DNA content in the cells. Researchers treated cancer cells cultured in vitro with a certain anticancer drug, and after 24 hours detected them with a flow cytometer; the results are as shown in the figure. May I ask: are all cells in the mitotic phase counted in peak a or peak b?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A flow cytometer can separately count cells according to differences in the DNA content in the cells. Researchers treated cancer cells cultured in vitro with a certain anticancer drug, and after 24 hours detected them with a flow cytometer; the results are as shown in the figure. May I ask: are all cells in the mitotic phase counted in peak a or peak b?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is labeled “relative DNA content,” and the vertical axis is labeled “number of cells.” The image contains two flow cytometry detection curves, the control group and the experimental group; both show two main peaks: peak a is located at the lower relative DNA content position, around 40; peak b is located at the higher relative DNA content position, around 80, about 2 times the DNA content corresponding to peak a. Then carry out reasoning: the flow cytometer counts cells according to DNA content. Before the cell mitotic phase, DNA replication has already been completed, so the DNA content of cells in the mitotic phase is 2 times that of unreplicated cells in the G1 phase, namely corresponding to 4C DNA content. In the figure, peak a represents 2C cells whose DNA has not been replicated, and peak b represents 4C cells whose DNA has doubled after replication. Therefore, cells in the mitotic phase should be counted in peak b.
